source.title: Generalization Guarantees for Neural Networks via Harnessing the Low-rank Structure of the Jacobian
source.authors: Samet Oymak; Zalan Fabian; Ming-Chen Li; M. Soltanolkotabi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how label corruption and training duration affect generalization, using a ResNet20 experiment rather than the random-label memorization comparison in V1.
record.gate_note: The study reports CIFAR-10 train/test error curves for uncorrupted and label-corrupted training, plus figure-only test-error trends across corruption levels. Jacobian alignment values describe a different property from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. The SGD/Adam comparison reports fitting speed and residuals, not held-out performance.
record.test_reason: The study explains generalization through Jacobian structure and reports clean-label versus corrupted-label learning dynamics, but does not establish V1's paired random-label memorization and natural-label generalization result. Its other experiments and theoretical bounds do not measure the comparisons specified by V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive conditional optimization and generalization bounds based on Jacobian spectrum and label or residual alignment. Their experiments show Jacobian adaptation during training, poorer alignment and generalization with corruption, and an early test-error optimum under 50% corruption. These findings do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness or optimizer generalization comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a three-class CIFAR-10 ResNet20 experiment with partial label corruption; it does not reproduce the random-label memorization comparison or architectures in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-corruption level and training duration change the reported test-error behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-label training and test errors decrease together. With 50% corruption, test error reaches its minimum around epoch 100 and then increases while training error decreases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued fitting of corrupted labels can worsen clean-test generalization after an early optimum in this three-class CIFAR-10 ResNet20 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher corruption levels increase test error and the portion of the label vector lying in the Jacobian nuisance space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label alignment with the Jacobian information space is associated with generalization across corruption levels in this setup.

record.problems: The empirical experiments use only three CIFAR-10 classes and ResNet20, with batch normalization disabled and a least-squares loss. The reported train/test error and corruption-level results are figure-only in the supplied text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper notes that the full Jacobian spectrum over the entire dataset is computationally intensive and that broader experiments were planned.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows omitted. Jacobian alignment tables and residual curves are not rows for V1 because they do not report the claim's test-accuracy comparison; the Adam experiment reports fitting dynamics rather than held-out performance.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside above-chance natural-label accuracy using the same recipe, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error; width-dependent theoretical bias bounds do not establish this comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning; Adam is compared with SGD on fitting dynamics and Jacobian alignment.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against competing measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No qualifying claim-version results are missing. Exact error values and chance-level performance cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The reported 8.75% ten-class ResNet20 test error is background performance, not a result of this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a paired comparison of near-perfect fitting to fixed random labels and test accuracy on natural versus random labels, or chance-level test accuracy for random labels.
No empirical width sweep past the interpolation threshold is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison is reported.
The SGD/Adam comparison concerns training speed and residuals, not held-out performance under optimizer tuning.
The study measures Jacobian spectrum and label/residual alignment, not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Train on the original CIFAR-10 data for three classes without label corruption; measure train and test misclassification error.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, three classes (automobile, airplane, bird); 9999 training and 3000 test images
standard data augmentation, e.g. random crop and flip

rows.note: The text says training and test error decrease together as learning progresses, but provides no numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Decreasing clean-label training and test error alone cannot establish coexistence with near-perfect random-label fitting. The plotted curves are unavailable in the supplied text. Values are minima over the preceding ten epochs, rather than individual-epoch errors.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Train with 50% of labels changed to a randomly selected different class; measure train and test misclassification error.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, three classes (automobile, airplane, bird); 9999 training and 3000 test images
standard data augmentation, e.g. random crop and flip

rows.note: The text states training error steadily decreases while test error first drops, reaches its minimum at 100 epochs, then steadily increases.
rows.check: Partial label corruption and subsequent overfitting do not establish V1's random-label comparison; 'partial' incorrectly treats a different comparison as an incomplete V1 effect. Test labels remain uncorrupted. Plotted errors are minima over the preceding ten epochs.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Train at multiple label-corruption levels and measure test error after 800 epochs.
rows.note: The text states test error increases with corruption level; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Increasing test error with corruption does not establish near-perfect random-label fitting or chance-level random-label test accuracy. Corruption selects a strictly different class: at 100% corruption, labels exclude the true class and therefore retain information about it. Test labels remain uncorrupted. Figure 9 also includes the clean-label baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
